== Problem ==

A board game spinner is divided into three regions labeled <imath>A</imath>, <imath>B</imath> and <imath>C</imath>. The probability of the arrow stopping on region <imath>A</imath> is <imath>\frac{1}{3}</imath> and on region <imath>B</imath> is <imath>\frac{1}{2}</imath>. The probability of the arrow stopping on region <imath>C</imath> is:


<imath> \textbf{(A)}\ \frac{1}{12}\qquad\textbf{(B)}\ \frac{1}{6}\qquad\textbf{(C)}\ \frac{1}{5}\qquad\textbf{(D)}\ \frac{1}{3}\qquad\textbf{(E)}\ \frac{2}{5} </imath>

==Solution==
The total of the probabilities of the arrow stopping on <imath>A</imath>, <imath>B</imath>, and <imath>C</imath> is <imath>1</imath>, so the probability of the arrow stopping on <imath>C</imath> is <imath>1-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{3}=\boxed{\textbf{(B)}\ \frac16}</imath>.
